{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Verified playbook findings on the Vendor's Master Services Agreement draft

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the MSA against our playbook. The draft is workable in several areas but contains a cluster of clauses that we cannot accept as drafted, and a number of them sit at or beyond our walk-away thresholds.

The three critical items are: (i) **no Vendor indemnity at all** — § 20 runs only from Customer to Vendor for "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services", with no IP infringement, unlawful-conduct, data-incident or wilful-misconduct cover and no claim-handling procedure (§ 9.3 even cross-references a non-existent "Section 20.5"); (ii) a **one-month fee cap applied "without exception"** in § 21.1, which is below our six-month walk-away floor and overrides the otherwise sound Excluded Claims regime in §§ 21.2–21.3; and (iii) IP ownership, which is fully compliant and needs no change.

The commercial lock-in provisions are the other priority. The three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay in § 2.1 "without reduction or termination rights" operates as a Customer-payable liquidated amount, defeats our § 9.4 convenience termination, and conflicts with § 12.3 (in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment). It is reinforced by a full-term sole-supplier obligation (§ 2.2), a worldwide 24-month post-term non-compete on us (§ 12.4), and a licence granted to "Customer alone", revocable at Vendor's discretion (§ 13.1) — each of which also contradicts other clauses in the same draft.

A good deal of the agreement already meets our preferred position and requires no redline: IP and deliverable ownership (§§ 13.2, 14.1–14.4), assignment and change of control (§ 24, § 13.3), audit rights against us (§ 22), governing law and New York venue (§ 28), auto-renewal and renewal pricing (§§ 8.2–8.3), absence of any MFN obligation (§ 12.3), and Vendor insurance (§ 18). One finding — non-solicitation — failed automated verification and needs a human read before we close it out.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 20 (§ 20.1; cf. § 9.3, § 21.3) | Only indemnity runs Customer → Vendor. Add Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, indemnity procedure and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies as § 20.5; narrow our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of law. |
| 2 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Liability cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Deviation | § 21.1 (cf. §§ 21.2–21.3) | One month of Fees "actually paid", "without exception". Raise to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 and subject the cap to the existing Excluded Claims carve-outs. |
| 3 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | §§ 13.2, 14.1–14.4 (defs § 1.4, § 1.8), § 15.1 | Meets preferred position in full, including present assignment of Deliverables and perpetual licence-back for embedded Vendor Technology. No redline. |
| 4 | High | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 (cf. § 9.4, § 12.3) | Multi-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right — walk-away. Replace with pay for what is ordered/used; fallback is a 12-month reducible commitment with true-up. |
| 5 | High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Deviation | § 2.1 (cf. §§ 9.3, 9.4, 27.3) | Take-or-pay functions as a Customer-payable liquidated amount for Services never taken. Delete; pay only for Services ordered and received. Fallback: early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount. |
| 6 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 2.1 (cf. § 9.4) | § 9.4 alone is compliant, but § 2.1's "without reduction or termination rights" may override it and there is no order-of-precedence clause. Make § 2.1 expressly subject to § 9.4 with pro-rata reduction of the minimum. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2.2 (cf. § 12.3, § 2.1) | Full-term sole-supplier obligation with no category, time or performance limit — walk-away. Make Vendor non-exclusive and preserve our right to buy from third parties. Fallback: single category, 12 months, automatic termination on SLA/delivery failure. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (cf. § 12.3) | Worldwide, undefined-scope, 24-month post-term restriction on us — beyond walk-away. Delete. Fallback: single named product, term only, capped at 12 months, with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs. |
| 9 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 13.1 (cf. §§ 13.2, 13.3) | Licence to "Customer alone", excluding Affiliates and contractors, revocable at Vendor's discretion — walk-away. Extend to Affiliates and contractors acting for us and tie revocation/transfer to the agreed § 13.3 limits. |
| 10 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 (§§ 24.1–24.4), § 13.3, § 9.2 | Affiliate and M&A assignment without consent; Vendor restricted; no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right. No redline. |
| 11 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Deviation | § 11.1 (cf. §§ 11.2, 11.3, 10.1) | Immediate cessation of assistance and permanent deletion with no export/migration support — walk-away. Replace with up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, with deletion subordinated to the §§ 11.2–11.3 return-and-certification process. Fallback: 90 days. |
| 12 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 19.2 (cf. §§ 19.1, 19.3–19.5) | Fifteen-day Deliverable conformance period with an express sunset that also strips the § 19.4 remedy. Extend to 12 months (90 days for Services) and delete the sunset. |
| 13 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Needs review (verification failed) | § 12.3 | Analysis found no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-inducement covenant binding us, and § 12.3 preserves our right to hire anyone responding to general recruitment. No redline proposed; automated verification failed, so a manual confirmation is required before closing. |
| 14 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 (§§ 22.1–22.3); cf. § 23, § 26.4 | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, Vendor bears costs below a 5% underpayment threshold, no direct system access. No redline. |
| 15 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | §§ 28.1–28.3 | New York law, exclusive New York County jurisdiction, no arbitration provision. No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | §§ 8.1–8.3 | Successive 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension, uplift capped at the lesser of US CPI and 3%. No redline. |
| 17 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 12.3; §§ 7.1–7.5, 8.3 | No MFN or best-terms undertaking runs against us; pricing constraints run against Vendor. No redline. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §§ 18.1–18.2 | CGL, workers' compensation, employer's liability, E&O and cyber/privacy limits match or exceed our position; insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities. No redline. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are identified in our findings as at or beyond the playbook walk-away threshold. We should not sign without movement on each:

1. **§ 21.1 — one-month liability cap "without exception"** (below the six-month walk-away floor, and it overrides the Excluded Claims regime).
2. **§ 2.1 — three-year USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights** (walk-away under MINCOMMIT; also the operative obstacle for LD and T4C, where the loss of an effective convenience exit is itself the walk-away position).
3. **§ 2.2 — full-term sole-supplier obligation on Customer** with no category, time or performance limit.
4. **§ 12.4 — worldwide, undefined-scope non-compete on Customer running 24 months post-term** (beyond the 12-month post-term threshold).
5. **§ 13.1 — licence to Customer alone, excluding Affiliates and contractors, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion.**
6. **§ 11.1 — immediate cessation of assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support.**

We would also treat the **complete absence of any Vendor indemnity (§ 20)** as non-negotiable in substance, given that § 21.3 already treats indemnification and IP infringement as Excluded Claims and § 9.3 assumes an infringement remedy that does not exist in the draft.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the ten deviation and missing items, with playbook fallbacks flagged in comments where noted (exclusivity, non-compete, minimum commitment, transition period, early-termination fee).
2. **Lead with the § 2.1 / § 2.2 / § 12.4 package** in negotiation. These are the commercial lock-in provisions and each conflicts with Vendor's own § 12.3 acknowledgement that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete or minimum-volume commitment — a useful lever.
3. **Table § 20 and § 21.1 together.** The missing Vendor indemnity and the "without exception" cap are interdependent: restoring the Excluded Claims carve-out has limited value until a Vendor indemnity exists.
4. **Resolve the internal inconsistencies.** Several clauses contradict one another (§ 2.1 v. §§ 9.4 and 12.3; § 2.2 v. § 12.3; § 13.1 v. §§ 13.2–13.3; § 11.1 v. §§ 11.2–11.3; § 9.3's cross-reference to a non-existent § 20.5). We should also raise the absence of an order-of-precedence clause and the empty operative text under § 23 ("Records and Customer Assurance").
5. **Manually confirm the NOSOLICIT finding (§ 12.3)** before closing it, as automated verification failed. We propose no redline there, since any edit would be adverse to us.
6. **Confirm commercial inputs** with the business: the acceptable liability cap basis, whether any volume commitment is desired at all, and the required transition-assistance window. We will hold the compliant provisions (IP, assignment, audit, governing law, renewal, insurance) as-is and resist reopening them."}
